meta.subtitle: AI weapons-screening vendor scaling a subscription base as losses narrow, still shadowed by a prior restatement

analystCommentary: Evolv Technologies sells AI-powered weapons-screening systems through a Security-as-a-Service subscription, and the June-quarter print shows the model scaling while losses narrow. Q2'26 revenue reached $43.8M, up 34.4% year over year, and FY25 revenue was $145.9M, up 40.5%. First-half revenue grew year over year while the net loss over that half narrowed sharply. Profitability is not yet here: FY25 net income was -$33.1M, diluted EPS was -$0.20, and the FY25 operating margin was -33.2%, an improvement on the -79.2% of FY24. Consensus is uniformly positive at 5 buys and a $9.85 target, roughly double the $4.91 price, but that enthusiasm sits against a real overhang. Management has disclosed material weaknesses in internal control that contributed to a restatement of the 2022 and 2023 annual periods and two 2024 quarters, and an ad hoc board committee opened an investigation into sales practices in September 2024. We rate the shares BUY with a $5.25 to $9.50 target range, a call more conservative than the Street while still crediting the growth and the narrowing losses.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Evolv Technologies Holdings, founded in 2013 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, develops and sells AI-powered security screening products in the United States and internationally. Its platform centers on two hardware products: Evolv Express, designed to screen high volumes of people for concealed threats such as firearms and large tactical knives, and Evolv eXpedite, an autonomous AI-based system for screening bags. Both operate only with Evolv's proprietary software and cloud services, and the subscription bundles Evolv Insights, a cloud analytics application that reports throughput volumes, alarm statistics, and system performance. The company delivers these through a Security-as-a-Service model with two sales models, a pure subscription where the customer leases the hardware and a purchase subscription where the customer buys the hardware outright, each requiring a multi-year, connected software subscription. Customers span education, healthcare, professional sports, live entertainment, tourist attractions, houses of worship, and industrial workplaces. Management points to Annual Recurring Revenue and Remaining Performance Obligation as the key indicators of the model's scale and durability, though neither figure is quantified in this pack. Evolv reports as a single reportable segment; FY25 revenue of $145.9M is shown entirely as one consolidated line, and the vendor breaks out no product or geographic mix.

thesis.body: The investment case rests on a recurring-revenue security platform growing 30 to 40 percent a year while its losses compress. Revenue rose 40.5% in FY25 to $145.9M and 34.4% in Q2'26 to $43.8M, and the half-year net loss narrowed sharply. Gross margin recovered to 51.6% in FY25 from 40.1% in FY23, though it stepped down from a 57.2% peak in FY24, and the operating margin improved from -79.2% in FY24 to -33.2% in FY25 as the base scaled. The counter-case is that Evolv is still unprofitable, with FY25 net income of {- -$33.1M -} and consensus modeling further losses in FY26 and FY27, and that its credibility carries a discount from a prior restatement, disclosed material weaknesses in internal control, and a 2024 investigation into sales practices. The stock at $4.91 sits near its 52-week low of $4.79, so the market is already pricing skepticism against a Strong Buy consensus and a $9.85 target.

catalysts: Continued reduction in the net loss toward the profitability inflection the subscription model implies.
Growth in Annual Recurring Revenue and Remaining Performance Obligation, the recurring-revenue indicators management highlights.
The transition of former Columbia Tech distributor demand into the purchase subscription model.
Onboarding of Plexus as a second contract manufacturer to add capacity.
Early international adoption beyond a mostly U.S. installed base.
risks: Material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting contributed to a restatement of the 2022 and 2023 annual periods and two 2024 quarters.
An ad hoc board committee opened an investigation into the company's sales practices in September 2024.
Evolv has not been profitable historically, and consensus still models losses in FY26 and FY27.
Loss of the Evolv Express SAFETY Act designation as a Qualified Anti-Terrorism Technology could carry reputational and financial consequences.
Warrants, earn-out shares, and founder shares are carried as liabilities whose value changes can swing reported results.

financials.incomeCommentary: Revenue has compounded quickly off a small base: FY22 grew 125.4%, FY23 50.9%, FY24 30.5%, and FY25 40.5% to $145.9M. Q2'26 revenue of $43.8M was {+ up 34.4% +} year over year, and the six months ended June 30, 2026 produced $90.1M against $64.6M in the prior-year half. The loss line has narrowed alongside scale. FY25 net income was -$33.1M and diluted EPS was -$0.20, better than the -$0.34 of FY24 and the -$0.72 of FY23. The half-year net loss {+ narrowed to $14.3M in 2026 from $42.2M in 2025 +}. Gross margin tells a recovery story after a weak FY22: 2.7% in FY22, then 40.1% in FY23, 57.2% in FY24, and 51.6% in FY25, with the trailing-twelve-month figure at 49.9%. Operating margin improved from -236.3% in FY21 to -33.2% in FY25, the trailing-twelve-month operating margin is -20.8%, and Q2'26 operating margin was -24.1%. Consensus expects revenue of about $182.4M in FY26, up 25%, and $218.9M in FY27, but still models a loss in both years, with EPS of -$0.08 and -$0.04. The management discussion also notes that revenue is recognized ratably over multi-year subscriptions, so a given quarter's bookings reach the income statement only over time.
financials.balanceCommentary: Evolv carries little leverage. FY25 total debt was $28.6M and net debt was -$20.6M, so cash and short-term investments still exceed borrowings. The current ratio has compressed sharply as the balance sheet was drawn down, from 13.61 in FY21 to 1.26 in FY24 and 1.23 in FY25, with the trailing-twelve-month figure at 1.18; liquidity is adequate but no longer the cushion it once was. Total equity ended FY25 near $0.1B on the vendor's rounding. The 10-K flags that the company's debt instrument carries affirmative and negative covenants, including financial covenants, that may limit operating flexibility, and that it may need additional capital to support growth. Warrants, earn-out shares, and founder shares are accounted for as liabilities, and changes in their value can move reported results independent of operations.
financials.cashflowCommentary: Cash generation is the encouraging turn in the story. Operating cash flow was negative across FY21 through FY24 but turned non-negative in FY25 on the vendor's rounding. The pack does not provide FY25 capital expenditure, free cash flow, buybacks, or dividends, and the dividend yield is 0.00%, so the company returns no cash to shareholders and reinvests what it generates. Trailing-twelve-month net debt to EBITDA is 2.8x and interest coverage is -9.7x, the latter reflecting that EBITDA remains negative even as cash flow improves. The company has said it may require additional capital to support growth, a reminder that the cash trajectory, not just the revenue line, will determine whether it can fund itself.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: On earnings-based multiples Evolv screens as unprofitable: trailing P/E is -245.5x, EV/EBITDA is -98.8x, and the forward P/E on next-twelve-month estimates is -64.0x, none of which is meaningful while the company loses money. The forward P/E on FY27 is not meaningful because consensus still expects a loss. Price to sales is the usable anchor at 5.2x, a multiple that assumes the recent revenue growth persists. The Street is uniformly constructive: 5 analysts rate the stock Buy with no holds or sells, the consensus target is $9.85 against the $4.91 price, the median is $10.00, and the range runs $8.00 to $11.25. That target implies roughly a doubling, a large gap to close for a company that is still loss-making and carries a restatement and control-weakness history; our scenarios sit below the consensus.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Revenue growth holds in the 30 to 40 percent range toward the consensus $218.9M FY27 line, gross margin stays above 50%, and the operating loss keeps compressing from FY25's -33.2% toward breakeven; the SAFETY Act designation and recurring subscriptions support a re-rating toward the lower end of the Street's $8.00 to $11.25 targets.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Revenue grows about 25% to the consensus $182.4M in FY26 but losses persist as modeled, with FY26 and FY27 EPS of -$0.08 and -$0.04; the shares hold a price-to-sales near 5.2x and earn a modest premium to the current price without the full re-rating the consensus target implies.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Growth decelerates or a control, investigation, or renewal problem resurfaces; with no profits to cushion and the debt covenants and capital-raise risk in view, the multiple compresses and the shares fall below the 52-week low of $4.79 into the mid-$3s.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: We weight the Base at 45%, the Bull at 30%, and the Bear at 25%. The Base at $5.75 assumes growth continues at roughly the consensus pace while profitability stays out of reach, so the stock earns a modest premium to today's price but not the doubling the Street models. The Bull at $9.50 requires both sustained top-line growth and visible progress toward breakeven, which would justify a move toward the lower end of the consensus target cluster. The Bear at $3.60 sits about a quarter below the current price and below the 52-week low of $4.79, and reflects the tail where a control or investigation setback, a growth stall, or a dilutive capital raise re-prices the shares. The probability-weighted fair value lands above the current price, which supports a positive expected return, but the wide gap between the Bull and Bear outcomes is why we hold a BUY rather than match the Strong Buy consensus. Our target range runs from $5.25 to the Bull price and stays below the consensus target.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Evolv reports one consolidated segment; FY25 revenue of $145.9M is shown entirely as a single Security-as-a-Service line, and the vendor breaks out no product or geographic mix. Within that line the offering bundles hardware, proprietary software, cloud connectivity, and onsite support and repair for the full multi-year term. Revenue comes through two sales models, a pure subscription where the customer leases the hardware and a purchase subscription where the customer buys it outright, each requiring an active, connected software subscription. Management has discontinued the former Columbia Tech distributor-licensing model, whose agreement expired December 31, 2025, and is routing that demand through the purchase subscription model, which it expects to lift product revenue and gross profit over the contract term. Because revenue is recognized ratably over multi-year contracts, reported growth lags bookings.

moatFactors.name: Switching costs
moatFactors.body: Each deployment pairs Evolv-only hardware with a proprietary, connected software subscription and onsite support over a multi-year term, and management describes typical four-year subscriptions. The hardware and software are designed to operate only together, not as standalone offerings, which raises the cost of leaving the platform mid-term.

moatFactors.name: Data and AI feedback loop
moatFactors.body: A large and growing installed base generates anonymized screening data that the company uses to train and update its detection models, which customers receive through software updates. The larger the base, the more real-world data feeds model improvement, a loop that is hard for a new entrant to replicate quickly.

moatFactors.name: Recurring revenue
moatFactors.body: The Security-as-a-Service model produces subscription revenue recognized ratably over multi-year contracts, and management points to Annual Recurring Revenue and Remaining Performance Obligation as measures of its durability, though neither is quantified in this pack.

moatFactors.name: Regulatory designation
moatFactors.body: Evolv Express carries a Qualified Anti-Terrorism Technology designation under the Homeland Security SAFETY Act, a credential competitors would need to obtain; the 10-K lists loss of that designation as a risk, so the advantage is real but not guaranteed.

businessMoat.durability: The moat is narrow rather than wide. The switching costs, the data feedback loop, and the SAFETY Act designation are genuine, but the market for AI-based weapons detection is, in the company's own words, new and evolving and may grow more slowly or differently than expected, and Evolv competes against new entrants and other potential competitors. The company has never been profitable, so the model has not yet proven it can convert its installed base into sustained earnings. Renewal risk is explicit: management flags that customers may not renew their typical four-year subscriptions, or may renew at lower revenue, and that returned systems that cannot be profitably redeployed would cause losses. A narrow, improving moat that still depends on reaching profitability is the fair characterization.

points: Revenue grew 40.5% in FY25 to $145.9M and 34.4% year over year in Q2'26 to $43.8M, extending a multi-year run of 30 percent or better growth.
Consensus models revenue of about $182.4M in FY26, up 25%, and $218.9M in FY27, so the Street expects growth to continue even as it decelerates.

The end of the Columbia Tech distributor-licensing arrangement on December 31, 2025 shifts that demand into the purchase subscription model, which management expects to replace license revenue with higher product revenue and gross profit.
International markets are an untapped lever: sales have been primarily in the United States, and management expects increased foreign adoption as it explores expansion.
The November 5, 2025 non-exclusive contract manufacturing agreement with Plexus is intended to add scalable, geographically diversified capacity to support growth targets.

management.leadership: This pack does not include an earnings call transcript or biographical detail on the executive team, so we assess leadership mainly through disclosure and board conduct. The most consequential leadership fact is governance-driven: in September 2024 an ad hoc committee of independent directors opened an investigation into the company's sales practices, and management has since disclosed material weaknesses in internal control that contributed to a restatement of prior periods. On the operational side, management has moved to simplify the go-to-market by ending the Columbia Tech distributor-licensing model and adding Plexus as a second contract manufacturer, steps aimed at margin and supply-chain resilience. The named executive officers and directors are listed in the April 2026 proxy, but the pack assigns no titles, so we do not attribute specific roles here.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation is oriented entirely to reinvestment. Evolv pays no dividend, the dividend yield is 0.00%, and the pack records no share repurchases. The balance sheet is lightly levered, with FY25 total debt of $28.6M and net debt of -$20.6M, and operating cash flow turned non-negative in FY25 on the vendor's rounding after four years of cash burn. That said, the 10-K states the company may require additional capital to support growth, and its debt instrument carries financial covenants that could constrain flexibility, so the priority is funding the path to profitability rather than returning cash. The discontinuation of the distributor-licensing model, which management expects to raise product revenue and gross profit over the contract term, is the clearest recent capital-and-margin decision in the pack.
management.governance: Governance rests on the April 2026 proxy. The board has determined that its non-employee directors are independent under Nasdaq rules, naming Kevin Charlton, Neil Glat, Henrik K hl (appointed February 12, 2026), David Mounts-Gonzales, Rajan Naik, Richard Shapiro, Kimberly Sheehy, and Mark Sullivan; Bilal Zuberi resigned February 10, 2026. All Audit and Compensation Committee members satisfy the committee independence requirements. In finding Rajan Naik independent, the board considered that he has no direct involvement or material interest in the company's relationship with Motorola Solutions. The board has no standing risk-management committee and administers risk oversight directly and through its standing committees, with the Audit Committee responsible for risk-assessment policies. There are no family relationships among directors or executive officers. The overriding governance concern is not board structure but the disclosed material weaknesses in internal control and the resulting restatement, which raise the bar on the reliability of reported figures.
management.insiderOwnership: Insider and institutional ownership is disclosed in the proxy as of March 20, 2026, against 179,355,563 Class A shares outstanding. Directors and executive officers as a group held 9,636,602 shares, 5.2% of the class. Among that group, Michael Ellenbogen held 4,557,005 shares (2.5%) and Anil Chitkara 3,188,455 shares (1.8%), with all other listed directors and officers below 1% each. Among 5% holders, BlackRock reported 9,391,975 shares. The Vanguard Group had reported 11,981,998 shares (6.7%) but, in a subsequent Schedule 13G/A, disclosed that after an internal realignment effective January 12, 2026 it no longer beneficially owns the shares directly, with its subsidiaries reporting separately. The proxy's share count is close to the roughly 179.87M shares implied by the current market capitalization.

idiosyncratic: Internal control and restatement: management has disclosed material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting that contributed to a restatement of the annual periods ended December 31, 2022 and 2023 and of quarterly periods beginning with the second quarter of 2022 and the March 31, 2024 and June 30, 2024 quarters. This history lowers confidence in reported figures until controls are demonstrably remediated.

Sales-practices investigation: in September 2024 an ad hoc committee of independent directors began an investigation into the company's sales practices, an overhang that can carry legal, reputational, and financial consequences.

Persistent losses and funding: Evolv has not been profitable historically, with FY25 net income of -$33.1M, and consensus models further losses in FY26 and FY27; the 10-K states the company may require additional capital, and its debt instrument carries financial covenants that could limit flexibility.

Subscription renewals: management flags the risk of losing recurring revenue if customers do not renew their typical four-year subscriptions or renew at lower revenue, and of losses on returned systems that cannot be profitably redeployed.

SAFETY Act designation: loss of the Evolv Express designation as a Qualified Anti-Terrorism Technology under the Homeland Security SAFETY Act could result in adverse reputational and financial consequences.
risks.systemic: Broader conditions bear on the model. Management expects results to fluctuate with inflation and interest rates on business spending, supply-chain constraints, public-health emergencies, geopolitical conflict, and recessionary trends. The AI-based weapons-detection market is described as new and evolving, and may grow more slowly or differently than expected, exposing the company to demand cyclicality it cannot control. Component costs, long lead times, supply shortages, and tariff volatility could disrupt the supply chain and pressure cost of revenue, a risk management is addressing by adding a second contract manufacturer. A portion of revenue comes from government entities, whose budgets and procurement cycles add their own sensitivity to the macro and political backdrop. As a small, unprofitable company, Evolv's stock has been and may remain highly volatile.

body: We rate Evolv BUY with a target range of $5.25 to $9.50. The case is a recurring-revenue security platform growing 30 to 40 percent a year with a gross margin above 50% and a loss line that is narrowing fast. Our probability-weighted fair value sits above the $4.91 price, and the Base outcome of $5.75 assumes continued growth without the full re-rating the $9.85 consensus target implies.

We stop short of the Strong Buy consensus because the risks are specific and material: disclosed material weaknesses in internal control, a restatement of prior periods, a 2024 investigation into sales practices, and no profits yet to cushion a stumble. The bear scenario set out in the valuation section is a genuine downside, not a formality. What to watch is the pace of loss reduction, evidence of control remediation, and traction in Annual Recurring Revenue and Remaining Performance Obligation; progress there would move us toward the Bull, while a control or growth setback would validate the Bear.
